records.key_result: Verification methods are claimed to automate complex verification tasks and support real-time authentication, without timing or cost data.
Deployed 22 real-world case studies in journalism, legal evidence, and history, archiving over 10,000 web pages.
The implementer reports archiving 10,000 web pages as an evidence base for DFRLab; this is an operational preservation output, not measured changes in public trust.
A cryptographic archive is claimed to have helped reopen a 30-year-old cold case; the case narrative is not systematic justice outcome data.
The framework identifies and claims to control provenance-data risks to privacy and agency, without incident or harm counts.
The demonstrative applications are claimed to make mapping and spatial analysis easier and potentially automated, without measured performance data.
The funder claims geospatial information remains openly accessible and censorship-resistant, without user or adoption counts.
Integrated Ethereum Attestation Service (EAS) and Filecoin storage into Proofmode, creating cryptographically signed, immutable, and verifiable location attestations for captured media.
The implementer cautions that proof metadata does not settle the reliability of the underlying content.
Five founding artists are named as participating in conservation and decentralized archive-management work.
Deployed operational browser-based prototype with Fission supporting authenticated decentralized cataloging, loan requests, and acquisition transfers.
The Trust claims to manage and grow digital-asset value, without artist-income or equity measurements.
The Trust reports maintaining artist proofs and stewarding committed artworks, without quantified conservation outcomes.
The metadata study identifies gaps in versioning, component documentation and conservation workflows that need resolution for the Trust Client's success.
The project claims that collected stories and curated collections are openly available as a data commons, without use or reach data.
The archive claims that communities retain control of their stories rather than surrendering control to institutions.
Akashic is described as preserving refugee narratives on Filecoin so they remain accessible and resistant to erasure, without systematic cultural outcome data.
The project claims data-generated value flows back to contributing scientists and communities, without amounts or participant data.
AI narration and physical interfaces are claimed to help participants connect emotionally with ocean ecosystems.
Platform fees are reported at 2%, with an additional claim of up to tenfold capital efficiency under community-managed project funds, not a ledger-isolating comparison.
24 community campaigns were live in Kenya and Uganda.
The implementer claims that a verifiable ledger tracks donor-to-campaign flows and shows resource use, without measured accountability outcomes.
The operational platform charges a 5% fee on routed yield donations.
GSR Foundation is the first institutional donor actively routing yield to Giga.
The partners assert that donor participation demonstrates institutional standards for custody and transparency.
Fees do not cover approximately $200,000 annual platform costs and Launchnodes subsidises the shortfall.
LIS grew from one to eight partners in one year and attracted its first institutional donor.
The proposal identifies uncertain future yields and the risk of premature project termination if pledged funds disappear; no realized harms are measured.
Cross-border fees reportedly fell from 28.8% for a $5 transfer to 2.02%; payment receipt took seconds, and fee comparisons are operational rather than participant counterfactual outcomes.
200 urban youth undertook microwork on the platform.
The executive summary reports highly positive participant feedback, but supplies no numerical trust or satisfaction measure.
95% reported improved quality of life and 80% improved saving ability; the summary supplies no comparison group or survey sampling details.
200 Kenyan youth were trained to access global digital microwork through a mobile app and wallet; this is a training output, not measured learning gains.
In phase two, all claims were processed within 24 hours, versus a pre-pilot average of 14 days.
Coverage amount increased by 27% compared with the previous season.
53% of participating farmers reported increased trust; the packet does not specify the endline sample size.
40% reported improved quality of life, with reduced stress and improved input purchasing among reasons; the endline sample size is unspecified.
One farmer reported replanting bean seedlings and obtaining a good harvest after compensation.
The first-phase account reports incomplete automation and manual claims-approval bottlenecks.
Yield of roughly 18–20% APY on a $50,000 grant covered incentives and daily pilot costs.
91% of merchants who made at least one prepayment continued using the service, adding money seven times on average over ten weeks.
All merchants who tried the service reported finding Sokowatch trustworthy; the survey sample size is not specified.
89% of active participants reported improved quality of life through savings, income and business efficiency; sample size is unspecified.
78% of sign-ups never prepaid, with lack of awareness or understanding and inability to save cited as barriers.
The product charged 8% APR, less than half the market alternatives, and onboarding and disbursement occurred within one day.
96% of participants were accessing this type of income advance for the first time.
Over half the borrowers used loans for business purposes, mainly livestock and inventory for additional income sources; the survey method is not detailed.
Over-collateralization was identified as a barrier for lower-income users and future scale, mitigated during the pilot by Cinch supplying collateral.
The stablecoin transaction model offered a flat 30 KES fee, against reported alternative lenders' average APR of about 67%; inventory financing is not directly comparable to digital loans.
77% of food vendors had not previously used credit or similar inventory financing.
The existing platform and agent network were claimed to have built trust during onboarding.
63% of surveyed vendors reported reduced stress; the packet gives the survey size but limited methodological detail.
The expanded pilot reports settlement under six hours versus 7–10 days, a reduction exceeding 95%; the initial pilot reports costs reduced to 2.5%.
The initial proof of concept disbursed 11,271 USDT to 262 pastoralists.
The expanded pilot reports participant trust with an NPS of 82; survey method and sample are not supplied, and respondents are not identified as donors.
Three-meals-per-day consumption reportedly rose from 13% to 77% and 64% reported improved unexpected-expense capacity; no non-participant comparison or survey method is supplied.
The payout-trigger methodology was changed to reduce susceptibility to cloud cover, indicating a mitigated trigger-data reliability risk.
Disbursement time fell by a reported 99.7%, from 3–7 days for MFIs to under five minutes.
47 VSLAs and more than 500 borrowers, 90% women, received $57,000 in credit.
The narrative claims increased trust through faster, cheaper credit, while also reporting trust erosion from repayment failures.
Credit is claimed to strengthen households, reduce dependence on male earners and ease income-related stress without systematic outcome data.
Borrowers reportedly used loans for school fees and climate-resilient farming; no quantified sector outcomes are supplied.
Principal recovery was 96.9% and full repayment 86.5%, with defaults linked mainly to liquidity and timing problems.
The implementer claims automated cash transfers and pre-disaster delivery, without operational timing or cost data.
The implementer claims delivery of digital aid to at-risk populations, without a reach count for this pilot.
The implementer claims transparent and traceable digital cash distribution.
The implementer claims reduced humanitarian impact from forecast-based flood intervention, without sector outcome data.
A secondary account reports 300 refugees using the payment system, but the funder launch text does not confirm achieved reach.
The secondary account claims privacy and auditability have been reconciled at the cryptographic layer, while acknowledging auditability remains partly theoretical.
A technical audit identifies an authorization flaw permitting a single-transaction drain of the aid contract's public balance; actual exploitation or remediation is not reported.
The platform was implemented with institutions in four Latin American countries across several sectors.
The team reports that UNICEF deployments support customer trust and ETC Labs strengthens technological credibility.
Issued verified educational credentials (university diplomas and college skills) and sustainability commitments with an international observatory.
Bureaucracy prevented consolidation of the originally proposed government use cases within twelve months and forced a pivot.
The implementer claims improved stability and faster network response without performance measurements.
Real-user pilot tests were conducted at three Bangladesh locations, without a user count.
The implementer claims the Dacope pilot ensured transparency, without supporting measurements.
Feature-phone users could not use the Android-only solution and asked for support during field testing.
Users can create savings circles within minutes and check status remotely on blockchain.
The funder reports reaching other countries, while a later independent account claims failure to scale or attract a user base; no user counts are supplied.
The blockchain is claimed to make savings-round status reliable and available to participants.
The funder claims increased crypto literacy among poor users without learning outcome data.
Users unfamiliar with cryptocurrencies were unreceptive, creating an adoption barrier.
The funder reports free operation, cash-out fees below 2 percent and transactions taking 3–5 seconds for Leaf and Kotani Pay.
Kotani Pay reached 15,000 beneficiaries in a year, including refugees and gig workers.
The solution claims the ability to ascertain transactions secured on the blockchain, without measured transparency results.
An individual UBI recipient reportedly established a garden, sold produce and purchased a goat; this is an anecdote, not systematic outcome data.
AidLink reported near-instant disbursement with 100% transaction success and an average cash-out time of 27 minutes.
The 2024 Nepal anticipatory-action implementation supported more than 4,000 households.
The implementer claims reduced fraud and mismanagement through automated fund tracking.
Live demonstrations experienced problems due to dependencies on SAFE multisig wallets and SMS providers.
The initial wallet onboarded over 14,000 users in two months; a separate case-study headline claims 4M+ people across 167+ countries without a reporting period.
DPGA recognition is claimed to have accelerated institutional trust and enabled government and multilateral conversations.
The implementer claims self-custody mitigates central-authority fund seizure and single-provider failure risks, without incident data.
Nexus Mutual created and voted on 149 governance proposals using GovBlocks.
The GovBlocks impact narrative claims that decentralization enhances transparency and accountability without result data.
High Ethereum transaction costs are identified as a reason for GovBlocks to expand to Polygon.
The implementer says low-cost xDai transactions helped reach basic-phone communities.
More than 40,000 user accounts made over 400,000 transactions during January 2020–June 2021.
Recording all transactions on blockchain is claimed to maximize transaction security.
The implementer claims emergency liquidity supported people and created new local trading connections during disruption.
The organization changed blockchain platform three times to reduce fees, with time and budget implications.
CHATS reduced aid delivery time by 80% compared with manual methods.
Three humanitarian projects reached 13,613 unique beneficiaries, including 11% children and 30% women.
The funder claims that direct transactions and secure identities ensured aid reached intended recipients with reduced fraud risk.
A beneficiary testimonial reports a reduced burden of children's treatment costs.
A beneficiary reported that her sick son improved after medication obtained through the project.
Deployments revealed insufficient architectural flexibility for diverse humanitarian organizations and users.
The platform is claimed to simplify healthcare-provider payments.
Health Pass recorded successful transactions by 39 users in the DRC.
Transparency and accountability in healthcare funding are asserted without result data.
One patient's testimonial describes quicker access to examination and treatment, without systematic outcome data.
Cash predominance limited adoption and validation, with digital infrastructure and familiarity identified as barriers.

blockchain_added_value.label: Asserted
blockchain_added_value.definition: Sources say blockchain helped, with no comparison.

blockchain_added_value.label: Descriptive comparison
blockchain_added_value.definition: Descriptive comparison with a prior or alternative channel.

blockchain_added_value.label: Tested comparison
blockchain_added_value.definition: Tested comparison against a non-blockchain alternative on the same outcome; only when the comparison isolates the ledger (rule V1).

deployment_status.label: Pilot
deployment_status.definition: A time-bound test with named users (GSR-confirmed, Gate 1).

deployment_status.label: Extended pilot
deployment_status.definition: Continued or enlarged by the same operator, still described as a pilot.

deployment_status.label: Scaled
deployment_status.definition: Same solution used beyond the pilot period with wider reach as routine operation (a deployment).

deployment_status.label: Handed over
deployment_status.definition: Used by a new operator such as a government, partner or country office (a deployment).

deployment_status.label: Discontinued
deployment_status.definition: Sources say the use case ended or the organisation closed.

deployment_status.label: Unknown
deployment_status.definition: Sources do not state what happened after the pilot.

evidence_level.label: Claim
evidence_level.definition: Describes what the solution does and why it should work. No data on results.

evidence_level.label: Operational
evidence_level.definition: Data on outputs, usage or operational performance, with no measure of user outcomes.

evidence_level.label: Outcome, no comparison
evidence_level.definition: Outcome data from participants without a comparison group.

evidence_level.label: Outcome with comparison
evidence_level.definition: Outcomes compared with a comparison group or non-blockchain alternative, without strong identification.

evidence_level.label: Counterfactual impact
evidence_level.definition: Randomised or strong quasi-experimental impact estimate, ideally independent.

implementation_model.label: Consortium
implementation_model.definition: Consortium = three or more organisations with named roles

outcome_domain.label: Reach and access
outcome_domain.definition: Adoption, active use, inclusion of women, unbanked people and displaced people.

outcome_domain.label: Sector outcomes
outcome_domain.definition: Health, education, climate adaptation, human rights and justice, culture.

outcome_domain.label: Risks, harms and unintended effects
outcome_domain.definition: Privacy, volatility, cash-out failure, exclusion, security incidents.

use_case_domain.label: Payments and cash transfers
use_case_domain.definition: Humanitarian cash, anticipatory cash, remittances, merchant payments, wages.

use_case_domain.label: Credit, savings and insurance
use_case_domain.definition: Micro-lending, savings tools, parametric insurance, guarantees.

use_case_domain.label: Identity, records and data integrity
use_case_domain.definition: Digital ID, credentials, provenance, archiving and storage.

use_case_domain.label: Climate and natural assets
use_case_domain.definition: Carbon and environmental credits, regenerative finance, climate data.

use_case_domain.label: Governance, funding and coordination
use_case_domain.definition: DAOs, community treasuries, crowdfunding, grant and donor flows.

use_case_domain.label: None fits
use_case_domain.definition: No domain fits; explained in a note. Connectivity and information access are coded here (rule D5). Counts toward taxonomy fit (metric 3).
